findings: Sources responded with deltaq0.208–0.234. In selected22-cell panel, DNp09 and DNa03 modulate already-active DNa01/DNb02; no new inactive downstream cells recruited at frozen0.001q threshold.

DNa02/DNa11/LAL013 remain subthreshold across all queried coefficients under DNa03 pulses. Direct excitatory edges exist; no sign flip found. Negative finding only applies to this dose/state/window, not all stimulation or all DNs.

DNb05 changes below0.001q still induce up to0.61/0.99deg/s change in original shadow motor command, biphasic. Integrated left+0.00519deg and right-0.02825deg, not real body turns; forward stays tonic.

Effective laws already include global historical volume scaling. Absence of normalization was an incorrect hypothesis, now corrected. No evidence justifies reapplied scaling or threshold tuning by desired turn.

Source time constants19–22ms; synaptic5ms.40ms finite stimulation and uncalibrated model-current amplitude differ from live experiments using seconds. A simple isolated filter calculation demonstrates attenuation but does not bound the recurrent model.

next_decision.instructions: Choose the most informative structural next action before another expensive organism. Preserve current failures and finite budgets; do not approve stages4/5 or choose by a desired turn. Prioritize a falsifiable distinction, not microtuning.

criteria.A_interface_identification: Use independently defined neural-to-body transfer tests to identify decoder timing/population mapping; do not fit gains to navigation or sham failure. Small DN changes have meaningful commands.
criteria.B_discriminate_excitation: First compare known physiological stimulation/response and current model kinetics to distinguish inadequate functional dose or state from an excitability/transmission model mismatch. Preserve parameters; an observed finite-window barrier is not automatically a defect.
criteria.C_joint_forward_turn: Design and separately validate a joint neural forward/turn interface using preselected populations; new connections to the reader require independent evidence, not just existing-cell modulation.
